speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs what is the Ministry’s approach towards the housing of transgender persons in prison settings in Singapore, having regard to the recent situation in Scotland where a transgender person, convicted of double rape of women, was initially housed in segregation in an all-female jail.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Isla Bryson was undergoing hormonal treatment at the time of his conviction to transition to a female.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In January of this year, 2023, Bryson was convicted of raping two women.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: At the time of conviction, Bryson’s self-identified gender was female.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: However, his registered sex was male and he still had male genitalia.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Bryson was remanded in a women’s prison while awaiting his sentence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That was done based on the Scottish Prison Services' policy, which determines housing arrangements based on an inmate's "new gender".

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The prospect of a convicted male rapist serving a sentence in a women's prison sparked public debate and concerns about the safety of the other prisoners.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In response, Bryson was moved to a male prison facility.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For example, for a male inmate who is transitioning and who has developed female features, such as breasts, it may not be completely safe for this inmate to be housed together with other male inmates.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There may also be situations where inmates, during medical examination upon admission, are found to have external genitalia different from their registered sex.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This follows ICA’s requirements that a person’s sex change must first be verified by a local relevant medical specialist before ICA updates the registered sex of the person in its database.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, may I ask the hon Minister for Home Affairs whether there have been any instances of transgender persons being assaulted, particularly sexually assaulted in our Singapore Prisons and what steps have been taken to deal with that?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And secondly, I wonder whether there is a regime put in place by the Singapore Prisons Service where transgender persons are regularly interviewed to see how they are faring so that we can make sure that they are safe in the prison environment?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the first, if he wants specific data, he can file a question and we can answer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, I would be surprised if there were many such instances.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But if he wants specific data, he can file it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is certainly not something that has come up in a serious way as an issue for a policy decision.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And Members can see how we take an approach which is slightly different from the approach, for example, in the Isla Bryson's case.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I would say ours is a very practical approach.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the second question, if you can remind me.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Of course, not all requests and concerns would be considered as legitimate.
